title: runtime safety playback and experimentation notebook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This notebook is a single-source reference for conducting telemetry-driven, safety-aware runtime experiments and playback analyses. It consolidates recommended protocols for: kernel scheduling experiments, deterministic request replay, profiling and sampling strategies, benchmark artifacts, and short runbook snippets to be used during experiment fallout. The intent is reproducible, low-risk exploration that preserves SLAs and traces regressions to kernel/service-level causes.

Scope and audience

- Scope: runtime scheduling, kernel-policy rollouts, profiling capture and replay, and associated experiment artifacts.
- Audience: runtime engineers, performance SREs, applied-ML engineers doing model-onboarding, and experiment reviewers.

Key principles

1) Safe isolation: always run experiments in a contained cohort (see Cohort checklist).
2) Determinism-first: capture inputs and environment metadata to replay exactly.
3) Cost- and SLA-aware: measure cost delta and SLO impact together.
4) Observability-contracts: attach structured annotations for every experiment.

Experiment preflight checklist (short)

1. Define hypothesis and success criteria (latency / p50, p95 / token-cost / qualitative output checks).
2. Reserve a cohort with traffic mirror or sampled shadow traffic.
3. Ensure telemetry ingestion (trace + kernel tags + kvcache metrics) is enabled and retention sufficient.
4. Snapshot model variant and kernel-image hash.
5. Create a rollback runbook with explicit thresholds.

Deterministic replay capture format

- Required fields: request_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id, model_id, model_commit_hash, kernel_image, input_tokens (base64 if binary), seed, env_snapshot (instance type, sequence_length_limit), header_annotations (priority, route).
- Optional fields: client_prompt_version, prefetch_hint, kvcache_warm_flag.

Example capture header (YAML snippet in text):

---
request_id: r-20251102-9b3c
timestamp_utc: 2025-11-02T14:22:10Z
tenant_id: customer-acme
model_id: redwood-mix-7b-v2
model_commit_hash: a1b2c3d4
kernel_image: kernel-v4.1.2
input_tokens_b64: "SGVsbG8gcmVkd29vZC..."
seed: 42
env_snapshot: g4dn.xlarge
header_annotations: {priority: hot, route: api-v1}
---

Telemetry annotation conventions

- annotation.runtime.experiment: <experiment-id>
- annotation.runtime.cohort: control|treatment
- annotation.kernel.path: <kernel-name>@<version>
- annotation.kvcache.warm: true|false
- annotation.rollout.step: canary|ramp|full

Kernel scheduling experiment recipe

Goal: evaluate a scheduler change that adjusts preemption windows and batch slice sizing to reduce p95 for short chat sessions without increasing p50 for long sessions.

Steps:
1) Setup: build kernel-image with metric hooks (kernel-v5-experiment).
2) Canary: route 0.5% of shadow traffic via shadow-routing to the new scheduler on a subset of GPUs (cohort: sched-canary-a).
3) Instrumentation: ensure per-token time series, scheduler queue depth, and kernel latency histogram are emitted with experiment id.
4) Metrics to observe: p50/p95 latency (end-to-end), kernel execute time, kernel queue wait, preemption count, token throughput, GPU occupancy.
5) Acceptance gates (automatic):
   - p95 end-to-end reduction >= 8% across short sessions AND
   - p50 change <= +3% across long sessions AND
   - preemption count not exceed 1.2x baseline.
6) Ramp: follow a 4-step doubling (0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50%) with manual review at each step.
7) Rollback: automated if any gate fails; manual postmortem if rollback triggered.

Profiling playbook (sampling and reconstruction)

- Use stratified sampling: 60% short sessions (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (128-1024), 15% long (>1024).
- For each sampled request capture: lightweight trace, kernel stack trace sample (every 5ms), and full kernel timeline for top 0.1% slowest events.
- Reconstruction: stitch trace + kernel timeline using request_id. Use noise-filters and a reproducibility seed to re-run captured inputs in a sandboxed runtime with the same kernel-image and model-commit.

Benchmarking suite artifacts and naming conventions

- Benchmark bundle naming: bench.<workload>.<profile>.<date>.tar.gz (example: bench.chat.short-echo.2026-01-10.tar.gz)
- Required files inside bundle:
  - workload.yaml (shape, qps, token-distribution)
  - environment.json (instance types, gpu topology, kernel-image)
  - traces/ (sampled traces)
  - results.csv (per-experiment aggregated metrics)
  - notes.md (experiment narrative and hypothesis)

Sample workload.yaml table (rendered as markdown in page):
| field | value | notes |
|---|---|---|
| qps | 120 | target ingress for load test |
| seq_dist | short:0.6, medium:0.3, long:0.1 | fraction by request |
| duration | 2h | sustained window |
| seed | 20260110-rtc | deterministic replay seed |

Release note template for runtime changes

- Title: [kernel] <short summary> (kernel-image)
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owners: team names + primary oncall
- Change summary: what changed and motivation
- Telemetry delta: new metrics emitted and tags added
- SLO risk assessment: p50/p95 expectations, rollback thresholds
- Rollout plan: canary percentages and time windows
- Known limitations: e.g., NVLink sensitivity, perf cliff for sequence > 2k
- Rollback steps: links to runbook and runbook ID

Runbook snippet: automated rollback policy

- Trigger: p95 end-to-end latency > 1.3x baseline for 10m OR error-rate increase > 0.5 percentage points.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Revert routing to previous kernel-image for cohort.*
  2. Pause autoscaling for affected cluster to avoid oscillation.
  3. Notify oncall (pager) and create incident channel.
  4. Pull last 30m sampled traces for triage.

Known issues catalog (experimenter-facing)

- nvlink-degradation-on-multi-gpu-batches: observed throughput drop when heterogeneous GPU clocks are present. Workaround: force uniform clocking or reduce batch size.
- preemption-starvation-in-long-sessions: rare starvation when preemption window aggressively slices long streams; mitigated by priority bumping for sessions with >2048 tokens.
- kvcache-warm-threshold-oscillation: warm hint churn can cause cache thrash in mixed workloads; mitigation: stabilize warm-hint emission to 1s buckets.

Post-experiment checklist

1. Aggregate experiment metrics and compare to hypothesis table.
2. Attach benchmark bundle and traces to experiment ticket.
3. If regression observed, create a regression hunt ticket with artifact links.
4. If successful, author a short release note and add to the weekly runtime-changes digest.

Appendix: quick commands

- Capture a sampling stream (kube): kubectl logs -l app=runtime-capture -f --since=2h > sampled-traces.jsonl
- Package benchmark bundle: tar -czf bench.chat.short-2026-01-10.tar.gz workload.yaml environment.json traces/ results.csv notes.md
- Re-run a captured input in sandbox: ./sandbox_runner --kernel kernel-v5-experiment --model-commit a1b2c3d4 --input trace-0001.json

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owners: runtime-performance (team alias: runtime-perf@redwood.internal)
- Escalation: cross-team SRE -> infra lead -> eng leadership if incident P0.

Related pages

- Link to the company benchmark catalog and causal-latency playbook (see related_pages).

Document maintenance

- Update cadence: quarterly or after any kernel scheduler rollout.
- Who can update: runtime-perf team and designated experiment reviewers.

End of notebook.
